title: Molecular interplay of ASNS and the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway in CMV and HIV co-infections: Therapeutic implications.
authors: Zhang, Hao; Yuan, ShuYou; Ding, ShaoXiang; Bao, HongXia; Chen, WenJun; Cai, Bo; Sun, JunKai; Zhu, HaoGang; Lu, Wei; Fang, Ye
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CMV/HIV共感染中ASNS与PI3K-AKT-mTOR通路的互作，虽含转录因子RUNX1结合ASNS启动子预测及分子对接/动力学模拟，但核心是代谢信号通路而非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，方法上仅简单应用，与TF-DNA结合机制研究关联较弱。
abstract: CMV/HIV coinfection markedly exacerbates disease progression, elevates treatment failure risk, and worsens patient outcomes, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood-creating an urgent need for targeted host-focused research. This study identifies asparagine synthetase (ASNS) as a pivotal metabolic-signaling hub in coinfection pathogenesis, with critical interactions with the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway. Using integrated bioinformatics analyses of transcriptomic data, ASNS emerged as a central hub in protein-protein interaction networks, with robust positive co-expression alongside key PI3K-AKT-mTOR components (PIK3CA, MTOR, AKT2, AKT3), while machine learning validated AKT2 as a critical node. ASNS was consistently upregulated 48 hours following CMV infection and across all HIV disease stages, while single-cell RNA sequencing localized ASNS and MDM2 to plasma cells in HIV-positive individuals-implicating their role in virus-driven immune responses. Transcription factor analysis identified RUNX1 as a central regulator: bioinformatics predictions confirmed RUNX1 binds to the ASNS promoter, and validation studies identified RUNX1 as the top biomarker for HIV treatment resistance (AUC = 0.714). Molecular docking and 200-ns dynamics simulations showed that cidofovir-an approved antiviral agent-binds ASNS with high affinity (-6.61 kcal/mol) through nine hydrogen bonds, forming a more stable complex than ASNS-ONL, with VAL-51 and ASN-74 as key residues. Collectively, these findings establish ASNS as a host metabolic-signaling hub exploited by CMV and HIV, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic target. Targeting ASNS, particularly at residues VAL-51 and ASN-74, may offer a promising host-directed strategy to improve coinfection treatment outcomes. This work lays the groundwork for experimental validation and the development of targeted therapies for CMV/HIV coinfection.
abstract_zh: CMV/HIV合并感染显著加剧疾病进展，提高治疗失败风险，并恶化患者预后，然而其潜在分子机制仍未完全阐明——这迫切需要对宿主定向研究进行针对性探索。本研究将天冬酰胺合成酶 (ASNS) 鉴定为合并感染发病机制中的关键代谢-信号枢纽，其与PI3K-AKT-mTOR通路存在重要相互作用。通过对转录组数据进行整合生物信息学分析，ASNS在蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络中成为核心枢纽，与关键PI3K-AKT-mTOR组分（PIK3CA、MTOR、AKT2、AKT3）表现出稳健的正共表达，而机器学习验证了AKT2为关键节点。ASNS在CMV感染后48小时及所有HIV疾病阶段均持续上调，而单细胞RNA测序将ASNS和MDM2定位于HIV阳性个体的浆细胞中——提示其在病毒驱动的免疫反应中的作用。转录因子分析确定RUNX1为核心调控因子：生物信息学预测证实RUNX1结合ASNS启动子，验证研究将RUNX1鉴定为HIV治疗耐药的首要生物标志物（AUC = 0.714）。分子对接和200纳秒动力学模拟显示，西多福韦——一种已批准的抗病毒药物——通过九个氢键以高亲和力（-6.61 kcal/mol）结合ASNS，形成比ASNS-ONL更稳定的复合物，其中VAL-51和ASN-74为关键残基。总体而言，这些发现确立ASNS为CMV和HIV所利用的宿主代谢-信号枢纽，凸显其作为新型治疗靶点的潜力。靶向ASNS，特别是在VAL-51和ASN-74残基处，可能提供一种有前景的宿主定向策略，以改善合并感染的治疗结局。这项工作为CMV/HIV合并感染的实验验证和靶向治疗开发奠定了基础。
